newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen firm in Europe, yen weak on all fronts.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen firm in Europe, yen weak on all fronts.

text.p: The dollar remained firm against the yen in European morning trading after pushing above 118 yen overnight amid broad-based yen weakness, traders said.

The yen dropped to a two-week low against the mark and hit its lowest level this week against sterling and the Australian dollar overnight. Speculation that German interest rates will rise before Japanese rates has sparked covering of mark shorts.

The benchmark Japanese bond yield fell to a record low of 2.065 percent overnight. Analysts said concern about the Japanese economy increased amid worries that the slide of many southeast Asian currencies would hurt Japan.
"The yen's weakness is due to more than just one factor but itis hard to see anything positive for the yen out of the Asian currency crisis," said Kit Juckes, currency strategist at NatWest Markets.
"About half of Japan's trade is within Asia, so its losing some of its competitive edge there, even though Hongkong and China are more important for Japan," Juckes said.

At 0750 GMT the dollar was at 118.22/32 yen, up from 117.80/85 in late Europe on Thursday. Against the mark it was at 1.8390/8400 from 1.8440/50. Mark/yen was at 64.25/27 from 63.87/90, while sterling/yen was at 188.05/34 from 186.06.
South East Asian currencies spiralled downwards overnight, hitting fresh lows from the Indonesian rupiah's move to a managed float system.

The rupiah hit a fresh low of 2,915 against the dollar, while the Malaysian ringgit recovered a touch but stayed close to post-floatation lows of 2.82. Other units in the region also remained vulnerable.
Speculation about a German rate rise is likely to intensify in the run-up to next week's Bundesbank council meeting, analysts said.
"This should tend to keep the mark relatively well supported through the early part of the week," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.

The dollar hovered around Thursday's European closing levels against the mark. Comments late on Thursday by Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum that the central bank was concerned about signs of continued consumer price inflation and that it wanted leeway on the repo rate had little net impact.

Dealers said dollar/mark regained ground quickly after a brief dip as the inflation remarks were seen as a rehash of what was stated in the Bundesbank's August monthly report published earlier this week.
